entries.comment: Samus: Samus's reputation: how troopers, Pirates, hunters and the Federation see her
entries.content:
Samus Aran is famous across the galaxy and known to almost no one. Per the original manual she was "the greatest of all the space hunters", credited with missions "everybody thought were absolutely impossible", yet her "true form is shrouded in mystery."

- Galactic Federation leadership: it hires her for what its own forces cannot do (Zebes as a last resort, Fleet Admiral Castor Dane's summons to carry the vaccine for the infected Aurora Units, ZDR after its E.M.M.I. went silent). The trust has limits; she destroyed the BSL station rather than let the Federation capture the SA-X (see Samus's defiance of the Federation at the BSL).
- Marines and troopers: mostly awe. On Tanamaar, soldiers pinned down by Space Pirates called out "It's Samus. She's punching through" and "I can't believe it. It's Samus. It's really her." Private Nora Armstrong admires her as a role model for her "famously unshakable demeanor"; Myles MacKenzie introduced her to a wrecked battle mech with "You know her. She's... she's famous." Some doubt the stories: PFC I. Crany of Bravo Squad dismissed tales of one person taking out an entire Pirate base as "fairy tales", on a par with "this Samus, or Bigfoot, or Santa Claus." On the Bottle Ship the 07th Platoon received her coolly; only Anthony Higgs greeted her as a friend.
- Space Pirates: to them she is "the Hunter", "the accursed Hunter, Samus Aran", a priority target with a bounty on her head (see The Pirates and Samus (the Hunter)).
- Fellow bounty hunters: respect laced with rivalry. Rundas, Ghor and Gandrayda fought beside her on Norion. Federation intel noted that Gandrayda saw "the veteran Hunter Samus Aran as her chief rival, a rival she intends to surpass"; once Phazon corrupted her, Pirate records say she "vowed to present Aran's bloody helmet to Dark Samus as tribute." The six hunters who raced her for the Alimbic power were rivals a Federation briefing presumed hostile, and Sylux hates her outright.
- Prophecy: the Chozo of Tallon IV foretold her as the Entrusted One, U-Mos told her for the Luminoth "You're our only hope, Samus", and the Lamorn hailed her as the Chosen One.

The legend runs ahead of the woman. Strangers expect the hero of the stories, or doubt she exists, and meet a taciturn professional who says almost nothing.
entries.notes: Every quote checked against a primary transcription: the original-manual lines (metroiddatabase transcription; the manual's 'he/his' pronouns are paraphrased away); the Tanamaar soldiers' and Myles's lines (Shinesparkers Prime 4 transcript; the soldiers are unnamed, and Myles is speaking to the wrecked MK-99 Betsy); Nora's 'famously unshakable demeanor' (in-game Biology logbook via OmegaMetroid); Crany's 'fairy tales' and 'Bigfoot, or Santa Claus' (Echoes trooper log); 'accursed Hunter, Samus Aran' (Corruption Pirate Data, two logs); Gandrayda's Federation data ('perceives the veteran Hunter Samus Aran as her chief rival, a rival she intends to surpass as soon as possible') and the Pirate log ('Gandrayda has vowed to present Aran's bloody helmet to Dark Samus as tribute'); 'Disposition of rival interests is presumed hostile' (Hunters introduction). The task's phrase 'the most famous hunter of her time' could not be traced to any official source; only fan wikis use it, so it is not quoted. The Luminoth have no prophecy title for Samus, so U-Mos's 'You're our only hope, Samus' (already in Prime 2: U-Mos) stands in. The 07th Platoon's cool reception follows the task brief and Other M: The 07th Platoon and the Deleter, which says Anthony alone was friendly from the start; no Other M transcript was reachable to quote it. Dropped 'Marine armor patterned after her Power Suit' because Metroid Wiki only says 'designed much like'. Kept to one clause each where other entries go deeper: Fusion defiance, Pirate logs, hunter bios, Sylux. Keys are all multi-word; bare reputation/famous/fame/hero are not used. No game titles in content.

entries.content:
Humans are the species Samus Aran was born into and the backbone of the Galactic Federation's military, research and colonies. The Federation Marine Corps is predominantly human, as are many of the people Samus has served and worked beside: her former commander Adam Malkovich and her old squadmate Anthony Higgs, Fleet Admiral Castor Dane, the Bottle Ship scientist Madeline Bergman, and the engineer Myles MacKenzie and the soldiers stranded with him on Viewros. Humans predominate on Federation worlds such as Norion, and no other sapient species appears as often in her missions.

Earth is humanity's homeworld. Its old stories travel with the Federation, whose warships bear names from ancient Earth mythology: the Olympus, the Valhalla, the Tyr, the Theseus. Per the original manual, the Federation researchers who discovered the Metroid on SR388 were bringing it back to Earth when Space Pirates seized it. Per the manga, Samus's birthplace, K-2L, was an Earth colony (see K-2L (Samus's home colony)). When Earth joined the Federation is not recorded, nor is the location of Federation Headquarters (see Daiban and Federation Headquarters), and no mission record places Samus on Earth.

Samus is human by birth, but not only human: the Chozo gave her their DNA when she was three, and the vaccine that saved her from the X gave her Metroid DNA (see Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become). Raised by the Chozo on Zebes, she rejoined human society when she enlisted with the Federation. Asked "are you human?", the accurate answer is: by birth, yes; by blood, not only.
entries.notes: The Metroid Wiki Earth page is an unsourced stub. Its claim that Federation HQ sits on Earth, and its real-world geology (iron and oxygen, seven continents), were left out. Its 2013 Human page is largely speculation, so only plain statements were kept: humans dominate the troopers and researchers, and no species appears more often. The Earth-bound Metroid shipment is in the original NES manual ('were bringing it back to Earth when it was stolen by the space pirates', per the metroiddatabase transcription). It is stated as a manual fact with no HQ inference, and the HQ location is deferred to Daiban and Federation Headquarters. The ancient-Earth-mythology naming comes from the trivia on the Metroid Wiki G.F.S. Tyr, Olympus, Valhalla and Theseus pages. Dane is human per his Metroid Wiki infobox. Norion's race is listed as Humans. The Zero Mission manual's 'Earth came into contact...' line could not be confirmed (it surfaced only on a fan Steemit page), so it was dropped. Keys: bare 'human' is omitted. The entry is selective (AND_ANY), so even 'are you human' needs a Metroid-context secondary hit. The core profile and the DNA entry cover a plain 'are you human' question.

entries.comment: Samus: Exotic materials: Cordite, Bendezium, Denzium, Talloric Alloy, Brinstone, Radion and Urithic Ore
entries.content:
Samus Aran's suit notes and scans rate the dense substances she meets by the weapon that breaks them.

- Cordite: a durable material the Chozo built with throughout their Tallon IV settlements, carved into statues and wall hangings in the Chozo Ruins and Phendrana Drifts that often hide Power Conduits; a Super Missile breaks it. The Space Pirates used it in their Phendrana labs, aboard the Frigate Orpheon and in the Phazon Mines, where a terminal logged steel hatch covers being "replaced with Cordite and Bendezium covers in two deca-cycles."
- Bendezium: an extremely dense material found naturally on Tallon IV and used extensively by its Chozo colonists. Only a high-yield blast such as a Power Bomb destroys it, though water supersaturation and microfractures weaken it. Samus met it in the shrines and tunnels of Magmoor Caverns and the gates of the Phazon Mines, and the Pirates plated an Elite Pirate stasis tank with Bendezium alloy.
- Denzium: a strong alloy on Aether and Dark Aether, akin to Bendezium and likewise broken only by Power Bombs. Per O-Lir, Sentinel of the Sanctuary Fortress, the mechanical sentinels he built, later corrupted by the Ing, fashioned it to block key areas.
- Talloric Alloy: a common material in drain covers, grates and tunnel caps met on her missions to Tallon IV, Aether and Bryyo, used by Federation, Pirate, Chozo and Bryyonian builders alike; one Morph Ball Bomb breaks a cracked piece.
- Brinstone and Radion: substances Missiles shatter. Brinstone shaped a Chozo shaman bust and pillars on Tallon IV, walls, pillars and a statue on Aether and Dark Aether, and a weathered cliffside on Bryyo. Radion is rare, found only twice in Phendrana Drifts: a grating made brittle by temperature swings, and the casing of fuel cells at a tower's base whose destruction opened the way to the Artifact of Elder.
- Urithic Ore: the primary mineral of Zebes's crust; planetary records (spelling it Urthic) call it ideal for subterranean construction.
entries.notes: Each material is sourced to its Metroid Wiki page, read as wikitext through the MediaWiki API, with scan data quoted from the cited in-game lines. The Phazon Mines terminal quote is verbatim. Cordite's column casing (Research Lab Hydra) is a Pirate lab, so the Chozo uses are limited to the statue and the wall hanging. The location of the Elite Pirate stasis tank is not given, so none is stated. Denzium's origin follows O-Lir's hologram ('The machines have fashioned a new alloy of considerable strength') together with his account of building the mechanical sentinels that the Ing corrupted. Metroid Wiki has no Urithic Ore page. The Zebes and Planetary Classifications pages spell it 'Urithic Ore' but quote the Metroid Prime planetary text as 'Urthic ore', so both spellings are keys. Weapon effects get one clause each; the mechanics live in Equipment: Missiles and Super Missiles and in Equipment: Bombs, Power Bombs and Cross Bombs. Order 90 as a glossary/index-type entry. 'Cordite' is also a real propellant ('smell of cordite'), a small misfire risk that was accepted because the entry's content is harmless.

result.research_notes: The Metroid Wiki's /index.php?action=raw returned 404 here. The MediaWiki API worked (https://www.metroidwiki.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=<Title>&prop=wikitext&format=json&redirects=1), and so did its search API (list=search&srwhat=text). Both give exact cited in-game text, which WebFetch's summarizer will not quote verbatim. Metroid Wiki has no Prime 4 character pages (no Nora Armstrong). Prime 4 lines therefore come from the Shinesparkers transcript and the OmegaMetroid Biology logbook guide. Unverifiable items were dropped. The phrase 'most famous hunter of her time' appears only on fan wikis. The Zero Mission manual's 'Earth came into contact...' passage could be found only on a fan Steemit page. The exact Other M lines on the 07th Platoon's reception could not be checked, because no transcript was reachable, so that point follows the existing 07th Platoon entry. The Luminoth give Samus no prophecy title; U-Mos's 'You're our only hope, Samus' is used instead. Minor inconsistencies found among existing entries: 'Samus: How she regards...' says Samus answered Myles's 'Teammates?' with a nod, while the Prime 4 squad entry's notes say the nod was removed as unsourced. Also, the Shinesparkers transcript has Myles say 'I worked on her back at base' about Betsy, which differs from the Prime 4 entry's 'a model he knew well'. Neither point was repeated here.
